name: Autosomal Recessive Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for HSAN Type II

criteria.description: Symmetric distal loss of pain and temperature sensation
Evidence of autonomic nervous system involvement such as anhidrosis or abnormal sweating
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in genes associated with HSAN Type II (e.g., WNK1/HSN2)
Lack of significant motor neuropathy or muscle weakness
Consanguinity or affected siblings consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of symmetric distal sensory loss and autonomic dysfunction with genetic confirmation of biallelic pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by clinical features and confirmed by molecular genetic testing.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal loss of pain and temperature sensation
searchTerms: loss of pain and temperature feeling in feet
reduced sensation to heat and pain

pathognomonic.notes: Due to sensory loss leading to unnoticed trauma
searchTerms: injuries that don't hurt and don't heal well

common.symptomName: Distal muscle wasting secondary to neuropathy
searchTerms: muscle loss in hands and feet due to nerve damage
wasting of distal muscles from neuropathy
shrinking muscles in limbs from nerve problems

common.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in affected limbs

searchTerms: low blood pressure when standing up

occasional.symptomName: Hyperkeratosis and skin thickening over pressure points
searchTerms: rough, hardened skin on elbows and knees
balance issues due to sensory loss
unequal pupil size with eyelid droop
signs of sympathetic nerve damage to eye
difficulty urinating or loss of bladder control

laboratory: Nerve conduction studies showing absent or reduced sensory nerve action potentials
Normal or mildly reduced motor nerve conduction velocities
imaging: MRI or X-ray evidence of neuropathic joints (Charcot arthropathy)
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in WNK1/HSN2 or other HSAN-associated genes
other: Skin biopsy showing loss of small myelinated and unmyelinated nerve fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement including renal and cardiac
Absence of pain insensitivity in early childhood

redFlags: Recurrent painless foot ulcers or infections
Progressive autonomic instability including orthostatic hypotension
references: Orphanet: Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy Type II - ORPHA:140477
Dyck PJ, et al. Hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies. In: Peripheral Neuropathy. 4th ed. 2005.
